resultados.refuerzo: Carnicería is the butcher's shop, the right place to buy meat.
Librería is the bookshop, where books are sold; biblioteca is a library.
Mucha agrees with gente, a feminine singular noun, so it takes the -a.
Vamos is nosotros of ir; vamos a plus infinitive means we are going to.
Compraste is tú in the past tense, matching yesterday's completed action.
Casarse always takes con: casarse con alguien means to marry someone.
Has is tú of haber, the helper verb in the present perfect question.
Alojamos is nosotros; -ar verbs share this form in present and past.
Alojar is the infinitive; the sentence needs a conjugated verb for we.
Funcionar is used for machines working; trabajar is for people working.
Un sello is the stamp you stick on an envelope before posting it.
Vago means lazy, the opposite of trabajador, which means hardworking.
Invitar a takes a before the person invited: te invito a mi fiesta.
Docena means dozen; una docena de huevos is twelve eggs.
Una cuchara is a spoon, the utensil you use to eat soup.
Por último introduces the final step, like finally in English.
Ir is an infinitive; por qué no needs a conjugated verb, such as vamos.
Yendo is a gerund; por qué no needs a conjugated verb, such as vamos.
Buena idea accepts the plan; it is a yes, not a polite refusal.
Una entrada is a ticket, used for shows such as concerts or films.
Apuntarse a takes a: me he apuntado a un curso, I signed up for a course.
Suspender means to fail; aprobar is its opposite, to pass.
Despejado describes a clear sky, with no clouds covering it.
Siglo means century; el siglo veinte is the twentieth century.
Estar is an infinitive; a lo mejor needs a conjugated verb, such as está.
¡Menos mal! expresses relief that something bad turned out fine.
Sabe is indicative; after no creo que the verb needs the subjunctive, sepa.
Ojalá takes the subjunctive, so the verb is haga, not hace.
Descansar is an infinitive; after que you need a conjugated subjunctive, descanses.
Vendrá is future indicative; after no creo que use the subjunctive, venga.
Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, so salgas is the right form.
Tanta agrees with gente, a feminine singular noun, so it takes the -a.
Tantos is masculine plural; gente is feminine singular, so it does not fit.
O sea que is casual speech; a formal report needs por consiguiente.
Acordarse de takes de: no me acuerdo de su nombre, I don't remember.
Cuánta agrees with gente, feminine singular, in this exclamation.
Hacer is an infinitive; after que you need a conjugated subjunctive, hagas.
Sentar is an infinitive; after que you need a conjugated subjunctive, siente.
Dar is an infinitive; after que you need a conjugated subjunctive, demos.
Prefiero quedarme en casa declines the plan; it is not an acceptance.
